settings.language.label: Language
signin.scopes.title: What each sign-in shares with AgentMux
signin.scopes.google: Google: your name, email address and profile picture (the openid, email and profile permissions).
signin.scopes.apple: Apple: your name, if you choose to share it, and your email address, or a private relay address if you choose Hide My Email (the name and email permissions). While AgentMux Cloud is invitation-only, choose Share My Email.
signin.scopes.neither: Neither gives AgentMux access to your Gmail, Google Drive, Calendar, iCloud or anything else in your account.
signin.panel.note: ⓘ Sign in to AgentMux Cloud in your browser — one account per install, no key to manage.
signin.panel.signInNoLongerWorks: ⓘ The sign-in for {{who}} no longer works. Sign in again to reconnect.
signin.github.needsCloud: GitHub tokens for your agents come from AgentMux Cloud, so this needs your AgentMux Cloud account.
agentPicker.filters.label: Filter the new-agent cards
agentPicker.filters.disabledHint: Close the open panel to change the filters.
agentPicker.filterBar.name: Name (A–Z)
agentPicker.empty.title: No definitions configured
agentPicker.empty.desc: Use the ⚙ Agent settings to add your first definition.
agentPicker.templates.hint: Each card is a harness (the CLI that runs the agent, e.g. Claude Code, Codex) — you'll pick which model it uses next.
agentPicker.templates.managedNote: AgentMux installs and runs its own copy of each agent CLI, kept apart from any you installed yourself (to run yours instead, switch on "Use the CLI on my PATH" for it in Toolchain), and keeps each agent's login and settings in its own folders. This isolates the tools, not what an agent can do on your computer.
agentPicker.notices.nodeHint: After installing, restart AgentMux and try again.
agentPicker.menu.label: Template actions
agentCard.updateTitle: A newer CLI version is pinned by AgentMux — update it in the Toolchain pane
agentCard.newSessionTitle: Archive current session and start a new one
agentCard.newSessionLabel: Start a new session for {{name}} (archives the current one)
agentCreate.duplicateName: You already have an agent named {{name}}. Choose another name.
agentCreate.hint: {{name}} is the harness, the CLI tool that runs this agent. Pick which model it uses below; the harness stays the same either way.
agentCreate.name.label: Name
agentCreate.name.note: Name it for its job, like Reviewer or Docs writer, so you can tell your agents apart.
agentCreate.runtime.label: Runtime
agentCreate.runtime.containerNoDocker: Container (runs in Docker) — Docker not detected
agentCreate.runtime.note: Container: runs in Docker, sandboxed. Native: runs on this computer with your files and tools.
agentCreate.runtime.nativeOnly: {{name}} can only run as a Native agent.
agentCreate.image.label: Container image
agentCreate.image.standardNote: The smallest image: the agent, git, GitHub CLI and Python.
agentCreate.image.developerNote: Adds Rust, a C toolchain, go-task and a headless display, so the agent can build and run projects (about 660 MB to download, on top of the standard image).
agentCreate.model.label: Model
agentCreate.model.note: Which model {{name}} runs with. Changeable later from the agent pane's runtime picker.
agentCreate.vendor.label: Model Vendor / Custom Endpoint
agentCreate.vendor.note: Redirect this agent's harness at a custom API endpoint (e.g. a proxy or alternate model backend) instead of the default vendor. Leave blank to use the default.
agentCreate.bundles.label: Bundles
agentCreate.bundles.note: In order: when two bundles name the same skill, the first wins.
